target_customer: Wholesale distributors and B2B retailers running legacy ERP systems
problem: Distribution ERPs are decades behind in demand planning, purchasing and pricing, forcing manual spreadsheet work.
business_model: B2B SaaS layer on top of existing ERP
product_category: ERP automation and demand planning for distribution

founders.name: Sam Oshay
founders.background_notes: Third generation distributor who spent about a decade in his family's wholesale business per Bessemer and the company; employers and education not stated.

technical_complexity.rationale: Two way sync with legacy ERPs plus forecasting models; deployment claimed in as little as one day.

defensibility.rationale: Embeds in customer ERP workflows and learns from their transaction data, but ERP vendors could add similar features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copy found through 2025; Dealroom headcount estimates fall from 46 to 25 (unverified).

market_need_then: Over 600,000 US distribution companies with about 7 trillion dollars in revenue run on lock in ERPs (Bessemer 2023).

branding.community_and_virality: Preferred software partner of Affiliated Distributors and ties to NAW and distributor user groups (company post).

brand_strength.rationale: Name resonates only in a narrow vertical; no brand press found.

outcome_analysis: Recurrency, founded by a third generation distributor, sells a layer on top of legacy ERPs rather than replacing them. It raised a 22 million Series A led by Bessemer in February 2023 and is still active. Funding after that is not confirmed, and labels of Series B in aggregators are unverified.
notes: Seedtable lists a 2020-08 seed and a substack says over 25M total with an Applico led round; neither corroborated so not recorded. Investor lists conflict across Dealroom (Sequoia vs YC Continuity) and Employbl; the company post is used. No dated competitor named in any source; the only named rival (Rootstock) appeared undated, so list empty.
